minutes.headline: Chair says the town's pooled trust funds are mismanaged and pushes for a forensic audit; no votes on spending taken
minutes.summary: The two-member Trust Fund Commission (one seat vacant) spent most of the meeting on the chair's account of a meeting with town counsel about the scope of the commission's authority over the town's pooled trust funds, an outside investment contract the chair called overly conservative, and an attempt by the state American Legion to claw back funds from a defunct local post. No votes were taken on money; the board set its next meeting date and adjourned.

budget_items.topic: Treasurer's pooled trust fund quarterly report (not received)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the last report received was the March quarterly and that no updated report has come since; he speculated the rate of return was unchanged.
The chair said Bartholomew Company (the private trust manager) raised concern that the pool is invested heavily in pharmaceuticals, which he called a problem.

budget_items.topic: Request to treasurer for full accounting of pool revenues/expenditures 2022-2025
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said he emailed the treasurer and finance director requesting all revenues, interest, fines, withdrawals and trading costs affecting the pool from 2022 to 2025, plus a full accounting.
The chair said the town holds a workers' compensation insurance fund under M.G.L. c.40 s.13A, tracing its authority to a 1913 town-meeting vote.

The chair recalled a prior discussion where a school committee member and a select board member found an unexplained sum in town finances that was never resolved, and argued a forensic audit is needed.

budget_items.topic: Bartholomew & Company investment contract for the pool
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair described the pool's investment objective form, signed in 2023 and never amended, as electing minimal risk and accepting returns that may not keep pace with inflation.
Richard and the chair discussed whether the roughly $2.2 million stabilization fund, managed by Bartholomew, is being treated the same as other pooled funds despite needing lower risk.

budget_items.topic: Schedule of fees and services from Bartholomew
budget_items.what_was_said: Richard said a prior fee schedule lacked context on frequency, giving an example fee, and suggested getting information on how often such fees are actually incurred.

budget_items.topic: American Legion / Post 283 funds - clawback demand
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the Massachusetts American Legion's adjutant is trying to claw back funds after the local post closed in 2013, which he told the town's attorney the town does not have to return.
The chair said that in the absence of a properly constituted school scholarship committee, oversight of scholarship gift funds falls to the Trust Fund Commission.

decisions.decision: Next Trust Fund Commission meeting set for September 11, 2025 at 5:00 p.m., skipping the usual second/fourth Thursday schedule due to member absences.
Review and approval of the August 14, 2025 minutes deferred to the next meeting.
Chair will wait until the requested accounting information is received from the treasurer and finance director before scheduling a joint meeting with Bartholomew & Company.

what_happened.line: The chair called for a forensic audit of the town's pooled trust funds, citing a past unexplained discrepancy in town finances that was never resolved.
The commission took no votes on spending and instead deferred action pending accounting records requested from the treasurer and finance director.
The chair said the outside firm managing the pooled trust funds, Bartholomew & Company, has the pool invested heavily in pharmaceuticals and under an overly conservative 2023 investment agreement.
The Massachusetts American Legion is seeking to claw back funds held by the town from a local post that closed in 2013; the chair told the town's attorney the town is not obligated to return them.
The commission, with one seat vacant and only two members present, set its next meeting for September 11, 2025, skipping its usual schedule.

why_it_matters: The trust funds under review include money held for cemetery, conservation, workers' compensation, and school scholarship purposes, so how they're invested and accounted for affects several town programs, not just one line item.
No money moved and no vote was taken at this meeting, but the chair's call for a forensic audit signals a request for outside scrutiny of town finances that residents may hear more about.
The scholarship gift funds the commission says it now oversees, in the absence of a separate committee, are a source some families or students may rely on.
